candidate_relations.reason: The episodic tachycardia arose in late pregnancy with normal laboratory and structural cardiac testing, but this category omits the junctional focus and isorhythmic AV dissociation.
A regular narrow-QRS tachycardia at 103 to 125 beats/min is supraventricular in origin, but independently marching P waves and variable PR intervals require the more specific junctional mechanism.
P waves occur at roughly the ventricular rate rather than rapid flutter activity, and variable PR intervals demonstrate AV dissociation rather than atrial flutter conduction.
AVRT ordinarily preserves a fixed atrioventricular relationship, whereas this ECG shows P waves marching through QRS complexes with varying PR intervals.
Transthoracic echocardiography shows good biventricular function and normal valves, excluding a cardiomyopathic explanation for the rhythm.
